Read labels at full sizeOriginal Supplemental Figure 4 separates schematic A, cadaver dissection B and normal-anatomy ultrasound C/D. C shows the superficial POL arm adjacent to the medial meniscal body and its merger with the anterior semimembranosus arm; D shows the tibial POL arm beside the anterior semimembranosus arm and medial meniscal posterior horn. The three POL arms are distinguished only in schematic A/dissection B. No MRI panel is present.
Identified in imaging panels: Posterior oblique ligament: superficial arm (C); Posterior oblique ligament: tibial arm (D); Semimembranosus tendon: anterior arm; Medial meniscal body (C); Medial meniscal posterior horn (D).
Identified in schematic panels: Posterior oblique ligament: superficial, tibial and capsular arms; Superficial medial collateral ligament; Anterior and direct arms of semimembranosus tendon.
Identified in dissection panels (B): Source-annotated posterior oblique ligament arm relationships; Semimembranosus tendon; Adductor tubercle. Cadaveric source photograph; not ultrasound or MRI evidence. Specimen age, sex and side unspecified.
Panel A depicts the superficial, tibial and capsular arms and their relationships with superficial MCL and semimembranosus expansions. It does not establish complete attachment footprints, tissue dimensions, independently measured anatomy or any patient-specific ligament integrity. B is a cadaver dissection; C/D are ultrasound and cannot satisfy MRI-only image requirements.

source_mri_full_resolution.caption:
Read labels at full sizeSource injury example in a 31-year-old man with recent knee sprain and full-thickness ACL tear. MRI B is a coronal fat-saturated T2-weighted turbo-spin-echo 3 T image: solid arrowheads mark thickening and waviness of the anterolateral ligament; an outlined arrowhead marks the lateral meniscotibial ligament beside its tibial plateau insertion. A is ultrasound from the injured knee; C is contralateral ultrasound with normal ALL appearance. The contralateral normality claim does not apply to MRI B or the whole injured knee.
Identified in this figure: Anterolateral ligament (locally thickened and wavy, solid arrowheads); Lateral meniscotibial ligament (outlined arrowhead at tibial plateau attachment); Lateral meniscal body (asterisk).
Identified in ultrasound panels (A): Anterolateral ligament; Lateral meniscotibial ligament; Meniscal body. Injured-knee longitudinal 22–8 MHz ultrasound. Separate from selected MRI B.
Identified in ultrasound panels (C): Anterolateral ligament; Lateral meniscotibial ligament; Meniscal body. Contralateral longitudinal 22–8 MHz ultrasound. Caption explicitly gives normal ALL appearance here; no transfer of normality to MRI B.
Only MRI B is selected for clinical-image scope. The author labels local ALL thickening/waviness and the nearby lateral meniscotibial insertion; one slice does not establish either complete course, attachment footprint, physical tissue dimensions or independently verified integrity. No statement in the source establishes the meniscotibial ligament as normal or injured. ACL rupture belongs to the patient context and is not directly illustrated or credited by this selected MRI slice. Ultrasound A/C, including contralateral normal appearance in C, cannot satisfy MRI requirements or transfer normality to B. Side, MRI slice thickness, voxel spacing, TR/TE and complete examination findings are unreported.
